key_insight: Trajectory replay preserves prior tasks while learning new ones by matching historical and incoming velocity fields, yielding density-weighted transport of their probability-path mixture.
engineering_relevance: It offers a way to continually update continuous-time generative models without repeatedly simulating full historical trajectories for synthetic replay.
method: Train an updated velocity field against a frozen historical field along historical trajectories and the incoming task’s field.
Balance retention and adaptation with a stability–plasticity coefficient.
Use mean velocity distillation to access historical trajectories with only a few network evaluations per update.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports better class-incremental image generation than generative replay and distillation baselines, plus two biological case studies across two modalities that preserve treatment-effect prediction.
watch_item: Practical retention may depend on the stability–plasticity setting and the accuracy of distilled historical trajectories; the abstract provides no quantitative error or runtime results.
paper_title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models
